notes.0-4: 'He struck the lighter' reads as either lit it (ignited) or thumbed its button (pressed).
notes.1-2: 'It struck her that the plan would fail' paraphrases as 'it dawned on her' or 'she concluded' (inferred) that it would fail.

notes.0-1: 'She raised a red flag at the meeting' can be a literal hoist or bringing up a concern (mentioned).
notes.0-2: 'The horse raised its head' = lifted (hoisted) or reared its head.
notes.0-3: 'They raised the shelf / the bar' = physically lifted it or increased its height or level.
notes.1-3: 'The report raised concerns about safety' = mentioned concerns or heightened (increased) them.
notes.3-4: 'The town raised taxes / revenue' = increased the rate or levied and collected it.

notes.0-1: 'The ad ran for six weeks' = was published over six weeks or extended over six weeks.
notes.0-2: 'She ran the column' = published it or operated (managed) it.
notes.0-3: 'The site ran the documentary' = published it or streamed (broadcast) it.
notes.0-4: 'The article ran 5,000 words' = was published at that length or amounted to 5,000 words.
notes.1-2: 'The service ran until midnight' = extended until midnight or operated until midnight.
notes.1-3: 'The river ran to the sea' = extended to the sea or streamed (flowed) to it.
notes.1-4: 'The list ran to forty names' = extended to or amounted to forty names.
notes.2-3: 'The tap ran all night' = was operating or streamed water all night.
